'''Nina Opanasivna Virchenko''' ({{Langx|uk|Ніна Опанасівна Вірченко}}; born May 5, 1930) is a Ukrainian mathematician, academic, author, and member of the Ukrainian resistance movement. While a student in Kyiv in 1948, she was arrested on charges of [[Ukrainian nationalism]], and was a political prisoner in a [[gulag]] in Eastern Siberia for six years.

On her return to Kyiv, she was able to return to university in 1956, going on to graduate school in 1961. She went on to study mathematics and become a professor of mathematics at [[Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute|Kyiv Polytechnic Institute]]. Virchenko was finally awarded her [[PhD]] in 1988, with a dissertation on integral equations. As well as mathematical studies, she has published on the [[history of mathematics]] and repressed mathematicians in Ukraine, as well as books for the general public.

==Early life and education==

Nina Virchenko was born on May 5, 1930, in [[Zavadivka, Ternopil Oblast|Zavadivka]], a village in Ukraine.<ref name="KPI biography">{{cite web |title=Virchenko NO |url=https://kpi.ua/virchenko-about |website=kpi.ua |publisher=National Technical University of Ukraine (KPI) |access-date=21 April 2022}}</ref> Her mother was a midwife and her father was a former officer of the [[Ukrainian People's Army]].<ref name="Dissident movement bio">{{cite web |title=ВІРЧЕНКО НІНА ОПАНАСІВНА (Nina Virchenko) |url=http://museum.khpg.org/1366623857 |website=Virtual Museum - Dissident movement in Ukraine |publisher=Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group|access-date=21 April 2022}}</ref> In 1937, the family moved to [[Chervone, Zhytomyr Oblast|Chervone]].
Virchenko attended Zhytomyr School No. 36. When she was a teenager, she gave herself the pseudonym Ужма (UZHMA), which was an acronym for Ukrainian—Woman—Mathematician—Astronomer. In 1947 at age 16, she passed the entrance examination to Moscow University, but enrolled to study mathematics at the National University of Kyiv (KSU) as her parents did not want her to move so far away.<ref name="Dissident movement bio" /> She joined a rocket and aerodynamics group, doing multiple parachute jumps.

Virchenko also became involved in the movement for Ukrainian independence from the Soviet Union, writing and distributing leaflets, which led to her imprisonment in a gulag for political prisoners from December 1948 to January 1954.<ref name="Dissident movement bio" /> When she was released, she was not allowed to return to university, and taught mathematics in village high schools. Virchenko was able to return to university in Kyiv in 1956, entering KSU's graduate school in 1961.

==Imprisonment and advocacy for political prisoners==

Virchenko was denounced to the Soviet secret police, [[NKVD]], and was arrested in June 1948 with a group of teachers and other students.<ref name="Dissident movement bio" /> She was imprisoned in [[Lukyanivska Prison]].<ref name="KPI biography" /> In December, she was sentenced to 10 years' prison on political charges, and sent to the [[Ozerlag]] gulag for political prisoners in [[Tayshet]], Eastern Siberia. Virchenko's forced labour included logging and working in a stone quarry.<ref name="Dissident movement bio" /> Conditions and treatment in the gulag were brutal. Prisoners were given numbers, and names were not used: hers was R-840. There was no radio and no newspapers, and prisoners had no writing paper.<ref name="KPI biography" /> Virchenko created poetry, which was shared orally among the prisoners, and she also taught mathematics, drawing in sand or snow with a stick.<ref name="Survival as victory">{{cite book |last1=Kis |first1=Oksana |title=Survival as victory. Ukrainian women in the Gulag |date=2021 |publisher=Harvard University Press |location=Cambridge |isbn=978-0674258280}}</ref><ref name="Dissident movement bio" /> She was released after six years because she had been convicted as a minor.<ref name="Dissident movement bio" /> She and her husband, who was also a former Gulag detainee, were subjected to KGB surveillance in a later wave of repression of Ukrainian academics.

Virchenko continued to support fellow prisoners, and were outspoken advocates on rights and the freedom and welfare of political prisoners. Virchenko was the Chair of the scientific and methodological council of the All-Ukrainian Association for Political Prisoners and Victims of Repression.<ref name="All-Ukrainian Assoc">{{cite web |title=ALL-UKRAINIAN ASSOCIATION FOR POLITICAL PRISONERS AND VICTIMS OF REPRESSION |url=http://museum.khpg.org/en/1163103067 |website=Virtual Museum - Dissident movement in Ukraine |publisher=Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group|access-date=21 April 2022}}</ref> In 2016, Virchenko was one of over 80 former Soviet political prisoners who co-signed an appeal to the Dutch public to vote in favour of the [[European Union–Ukraine Association Agreement|European Union-Ukraine Association Agreement]].<ref name="Euromaidan Press 2016">{{cite news |title=Former Soviet political prisoners appeal to the Dutch for a YES-vote |url=https://euromaidanpress.com/2016/03/11/90204/ |access-date=21 April 2022 |agency=Euromaidan Press |date=11 March 2016}}</ref>

Virchenko had been interested in the work of Ukrainian mathematician [[Mikhail Kravchuk]] for some time. When she learned that he had died in a gulag, she began studying his life and mathematical legacy.<ref name="KPI biography" /> She wrote a book about him,<ref name="Giant of UKR Mathematics">{{cite book |last1=Virchenko |first1=NO |title=Велет української математики ("The Giant of Ukrainian Mathematics") |date=2012 |publisher=Scientific World |location=Kyiv |edition=2nd |url=http://irbis-nbuv.gov.ua/ulib/item/0001899 |access-date=29 April 2022}}</ref> organized a series of international mathematical meetings in his honor from 1992, the 100th anniversary of his birth,<ref name="Kravchuk conference">{{cite web |title=Відкриття XVІ Міжнародної наукової конференції імені академіка Михайла Кравчука {{!}} КПІ ім. Ігоря Сікорського |url=http://kpi.ua/kravchuk-15 |website=kpi.ua |access-date=29 April 2022}}</ref> and advocated for a monument in his honor.<ref name="KPI biography" /> Virchenko was also the scientific advisor for a documentary [[Oleksandr Riabokrys]], called "Голгофа академіка Кравчука" (Academic Kravchuk Calvary).<ref name="Kravchuk documentary">{{cite web |title=Голгофа академіка Кравчука|url=https://tv.suspilne.media/video/5413 |website=tv.suspilne.media |access-date=22 April 2022 |language=uk}}</ref> Riabokrys also filmed a short documentary about Virchenko, titled ужма<ref name="ужма">{{cite web |last1=Riabokrys |first1=Oleksandr |title=ужма (UZHMA) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h9cXw1UtlME |website=YouTube |access-date=29 April 2022}}</ref> (UZMA).

==Academic career==

In 1965, Virchenko became an assistant professor in mathematics at KSU. From 1974 to 1990, she was an assistant professor of mathematics at then National Technical University of Ukraine (now called [[Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute]]), promoted to professor in 1990.<ref name="Mathnet">{{cite web |title=Persons: Virchenko, Nina Opanasivna |url=http://www.mathnet.ru/eng/person41511 |website=www.mathnet.ru |access-date=22 April 2022}}</ref> She was awarded a PhD in 1988,<ref name="Encyclopedia of Modern Ukraine">{{cite web |title=Virchenko, Nina Opanasivna |url=https://esu.com.ua/search_articles.php?id=34731 |website=Encyclopedia of Modern Ukraine |publisher=National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine |access-date=29 April 2022}}</ref> for her dissertation, ''Dual (Triple) Integral Equations'' (in Russian).<ref name="Dissertation 1989">{{cite book |last1=Virchenko |first1=NO |title=Dual (Triple) Integral Equations [in Russian] |date=1989 |publisher=Vishcha Shkola, Izd |location=Kyiv}}</ref>
Virchenko's studies included special functions, integral equations, and partial differential equations.<ref name="Mathnet-ru">{{cite web |title=Persons: Virchenko, Nina Opanasivna |url=http://www.mathnet.ru/eng/person41511 |website=Math-Net.Ru |access-date=29 April 2022}}</ref>

As well as over 350 scientific publications in mathematics,<ref name="KPI biography" /> Virchenko has published articles and books on the history of mathematics, including for the general public.<ref name="Encyclopedia of Modern Ukraine" /> This includes a book on mathematical aphorisms and quotes, published in three languages.<ref name="KPI biography" /> Virchenko also published a memoir in 2011.<ref name="Memoir">{{cite book |last1=Virchenko |first1=Nina |title=[Grains from the roads of my life] |date=2011 |publisher=Zadruga |language=Ukrainian}}</ref>

She has received several awards and honours, including the Yaroslav the Wise Award from the Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (1999), medal "Building of Ukraine" (2001), Medal of Andrew the First-Called (2005), badge from the Ministry of Education and Science "Petro Mohyla" (2007), and Honored Worker of Education of Ukraine (2006).<ref name="KPI biography" />

==Personal life==

Virchenko married writer and translator [[Rostyslav Dotsenko]] (19 April 1931 – 24 October 2012) in 1964.<ref name="Dissident movement bio" /> Dotsenko was also a former political prisoner. They had two children.
